differences.title: 1. STORAGE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Stores values by column in contiguous memory chunks, executing SIMD vectorized scans across millions of rows per millisecond.
differences.rightDesc: Stores full rows contiguously inside standard B-Tree pages, optimal for single-record key lookups.

differences.title: 2. TARGET WORKLOAD
differences.leftDesc: Built specifically for analytical queries like GROUP BY, window functions, and complex joins over gigabytes of Parquet.
differences.rightDesc: Designed for high-throughput single-row transactional writes, reads, and primary key point operations.

differences.title: 3. PARQUET & ARROW
differences.leftDesc: Queries remote Parquet, JSON, and Apache Arrow streams directly without loading data into an internal database file.
differences.rightDesc: Requires virtual table extensions and data loading scripts to parse and index external analytical formats.

differences.title: 4. MULTI-THREADING
differences.leftDesc: Saturates all CPU cores automatically with a morsel-driven parallel query engine for batch workloads.
differences.rightDesc: Serializes concurrent writes using WAL locks, limiting concurrent execution throughput on heavy calculations.

differences.title: 5. MEMORY CONSUMPTION
differences.leftDesc: Allocates large RAM buffer pools and spills intermediate group states to temporary disk when memory limits are reached.
differences.rightDesc: Runs smoothly inside embedded IoT devices, mobile apps, and smart watches with minimal megabytes of memory.

differences.title: 6. QUERY OPTIMIZER
differences.leftDesc: Advanced vectorized optimizer calculates join order reordering, filter pushdown, and dynamic runtime statistics.
differences.rightDesc: Lean query planner prioritizing predictable, deterministic execution plans and zero runtime overhead.

differences.title: 7. PRIMARY USE-CASE
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for Python Pandas replacements, dashboard aggregation engines, and local data warehouse experiments.
differences.rightDesc: The undisputed gold standard for edge devices, browser caches, desktop apps, and microservice databases.
